$comment: GENERATED companion to docs/radio-addressing.md. That document is normative; this file is the machine-readable contract other repos assert against. Do not hand-edit.

algorithm.decode: n = 0; for p in 0..4: n = n*5 + index_in_alphabet(name[p])
algorithm.normalize: trim ASCII whitespace; map A-Z to a-z
algorithm.encode: n -> name, the inverse of decode: for p = 4 down to 0: name[p] = alphabet(p)[n % 5]; n = n / 5
algorithm.endianness: name[0] is the MOST significant base-5 digit and name[4] the LEAST. Base-5 conversion naturally emits least-significant first, so a naive encoder produces reversed names: n=1 is 'zuzuv', not 'vuzuz'. The error is diagnostic-free -- 3125 well-formed, regex-passing, distinct names in the wrong order.
algorithm.reject_non_cvcvc: A name outside ^[zvgpt][uoiea][zvgpt][uoiea][zvgpt]$ after normalize has NO address and MUST raise. Never fall back to a hash, a default, or a truncation: base5 is undefined outside the codebook, and inventing an address is the silent-failure class this whole scheme exists to remove. Applies to !N and to every host tool.
algorithm.malformed_vs_unknown: MALFORMED (outside the accept regex) must raise -- no address exists. WELL-FORMED BUT UNKNOWN (a valid CVCVC name no board currently uses) must be ACCEPTED -- it is a legal retune to a quiet pair. The address layer does not know which boards exist and must not pretend to; that is the deploy-time silicon gate's job. Rejecting the second breaks tune-to-whatever-I-name; accepting the first yields a working-looking link on an arbitrary channel. Both failures are silent, in opposite directions.

channel.note: 25 is a VALID channel and zeguz occupies it

why.10: microbit-radio-relay's !C button space forces group 10 across channels 0-35

properties.full_space_canonical_form: for n = 0..3124 in order, one line '<name>,<channel>,<group>\n', UTF-8, sha256 of the concatenation

endianness_probe.why: Digit-palindrome names are IDENTICAL under both orderings and cannot detect a reversed encoder. zuzuz, tatat, zotoz and pipip are all palindromes -- including both extremes, which is what an implementer reaches for first. zotuz (n=225) reverses to zutoz and is the published vector that catches it.
endianness_probe.reversed_encoder_digest_note: If your digest equals THIS value, your encoder is little-endian; reverse the digit order.

properties.full_space_sha256_note: D1 -- FORWARD ONLY. Covers encode(n->name) and addr(n->pair). It does NOT call decode(name->n) or reverse(pair->n): a build with both of those broken produces a byte-identical D1. Keep it as a diagnostic bisector -- D2 failing while D1 passes localises the fault to decode/reverse -- but D2 is the conformance gate.
properties.conformance_sha256_note: D2 -- PRIMARY conformance constant. Canonical form: for n = 0..3124 in order, one line '<name>,<channel>,<group>,<decode(name)>,<reverse(channel,group)>\n', UTF-8, sha256 of the concatenation. The last two columns are always n, which is the point: every line forces decode() and reverse() to run and hashes their output. decode() is the PRODUCTION path -- it is what the relay's !N <name> executes on every command. A little-endian decoder is wrong on 3000 of 3125 names (96%) and passes D1; against D2 it yields 2e4e9013... and fails loudly.

conformance_sha256_broken_decode.fault: EXACTLY ONE fault: decode() reads name[0] as the LEAST significant base-5 digit (little-endian) while encode(), addr() and reverse() are all correct. That decoder is wrong on 3000 of 3125 names (96%) and produces a byte-identical D1.
conformance_sha256_broken_decode.use: If an implementation's D2 equals this, its decoder is little-endian: reverse the digit order. A previous revision published the prefix 2e4e9013 for a DOUBLE fault (little-endian decode AND reverse() returning 0) without specifying the variant, which made it unreproducible from the spec and therefore useless as a diagnostic. Reported by pxt-nezha-diffdrive-4f, who tried six reconstructions and could not regenerate it.

dump_protocol.v1: 3 columns '<name>,<channel>,<group>' -- digests to D1. Accepted; does not exercise the inverse.
dump_protocol.v2: 5 columns '<name>,<channel>,<group>,<decode(name)>,<reverse(channel,group)>' -- digests to D2. PREFERRED. A checker can tell them apart by counting columns. v2 puts the inverse INTO the hashed artifact rather than trusting each dumper's internal self-check.

vectors.name: zuzuv
vectors.note: n=1, the simplest ASYMMETRIC vector: reverses to vuzuz, so it fails loudly against a little-endian encoder where zuzuz and tatat both pass

vectors.name: zotuz
vectors.note: group-skip boundary; would have been group 10

vectors.name: zotoz
